title: Natural regular SL2 representations over a ring
statement: Let $B$ be a commutative ring, and $V$ a $B$-module. Tensor products mean [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. A natural regular representation of $\operatorname{SL}_{2,B}$ on a finite free module is a family of group homomorphisms $\rho_C:\operatorname{SL}_2(C)\to\operatorname{Aut}_C(C\otimes_B V)$ for all commutative $B$-algebras $C$ [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient], where $\operatorname{SL}_2(C)$ consists of the $2\times2$ matrices of determinant one [def-weil-pbc-matrix-determinant]. For every $B$-algebra map $f:C\to D$, the canonical tensor map $f\otimes\mathrm{id}_V$ intertwines $\rho_C(g)$ with $\rho_D(f(g))$. Regularity means that there exist $n\geq0$, a basis $b_1,\ldots,b_n$ of $V$ [def-weil-pbc-free-module], and polynomials $p_{ij}\in B[x_{00},x_{01},x_{10},x_{11}]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] such that for every $C$ and $g\in\operatorname{SL}_2(C)$, the $i$-th coordinate of $\rho_C(g)(1\otimes b_j)$ in the scalar-extended basis is $p_{ij}(g_{00},g_{01},g_{10},g_{11})$. Thus the entries are regular functions modulo $x_{00}x_{11}-x_{01}x_{10}-1$; representatives need only exist. Write $x_+(z)=I+zE_{12}$, $x_-(z)=I+zE_{21}$, $w=x_+(1)x_-(-1)x_+(1)$ and $h(t)=\mathrm{diag}(t,t^{-1})$ for a unit $t$; equivalently $h(t)=x_+(t)x_-(-t^{-1})x_+(t)w^{-1}$.
